summary: Helmut Rix worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Würzburg, Heidelberg (PhD), and Tübingen (Habilitation). He held posts at Tübingen, Augustana-Hochschule Neuendettelsau (1955), the University of Regensburg (1966), and as professor at the University of Freiburg (1982–1993).

Helmut Tauscher is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Ernst Steinkellner. He held posts as professor at the University of Vienna (attested 2010–2015) and as Numata visiting professor at Leiden University.

Helmuth von Glasenapp worked in Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tübingen, Munich, Bonn (PhD, Habilitation), and Berlin under Hermann Jacobi and others. He held academic posts at Bonn, Berlin, Königsberg (1928–1944), and Tübingen (1946–1959).

Helwig Schmidt-Glintzer is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Göttingen (~1967–1969) and the University of Munich (~1969–1973), later holding posts at Munich (~1979–1993) and Göttingen (~1993–2015).
Hemchandra Raychaudhuri worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He served as Carmichael Professor and department head at the University of Calcutta, with posts attested in 1939 and 1965.

Henepola Gunaratana works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Vidyasekhara Pirivena, Vidyalankara Pirivena, Buddhist Missionary College, and American University (BA, PhD). He held positions at the Buddhist Institute of Kuala Lumpur, Washington Buddhist Vihara, and several American universities.

Heng Sure is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Oakland University, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union (PhD) under Ronald Y. Nakasone and Hsuan Hua. He has held professorships at Bond University, Dharma Realm Buddhist University, and GTU.

Henk Blezer is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed his doctoraal studies at Leiden University (1987–1997), where he was a postdoctoral researcher and teacher, and also held a post at the International Institute for Asian Studies (1997–2001).

Henk Bodewitz was an Indologist who completed his degrees and PhD under Jan Gonda at Utrecht University. He served as assistant professor and chair of Sanskrit at Utrecht University (1966–1992) and as professor at Leiden University (~1976; 1992–2002).

Henri Bergson was a philosopher who studied at the Lycée Condorcet, École Normale Supérieure (~1878–1881), and University of Paris. His career included posts at the Lycée David d'Angers (~1881–1883) and the Collège de France (1900–1904).

Henri Cordier was a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology who studied at Lycée Chaptal. He served as a professor at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1881–1925) and at Sciences Po (~1886–1925).

Henri Gaidoz studied at Collège Louis-le-Grand and under Albrecht Weber (1865). He taught geography and ethnography at Sciences Po (1872–1908) and served as directeur d’études for Celtic philology at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from 1876.

Henri Hubert specialized in religious studies and history/archaeology, studying at Collège Louis-le-Grand and École Normale Supérieure. He held posts at the National Archaeological Museum (~1898–1927), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1901–1927), and École du Louvre (~1906–1927).

Henri Maspero specialized in Sinology, religious studies, and linguistics. He studied at institutions including INALCO and under Édouard Chavannes. His posts included the École Française d'Extrême-Orient, Collège de France (1918–1945), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1927–1944), and the University of Paris.
Henri Massé was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He held academic posts at the University of Algiers (~1919–1927) and the École des Langues Orientales (~1927–1958).

Henri Pirenne was a historian who studied at the universities of Liège, Ghent, Berlin, Leipzig, and Paris, as well as the EPHE. He held posts at the University of Liège (~1885–1886) and Ghent University (1886–1931) as professor of history.

Henrik Samuel Nyberg worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Uppsala University (1908) and held posts at the Fjellstedt School (~1912–1919) and Uppsala University (~1919–1956) as dozent and professor in Semitics.

Henry Beveridge worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Glasgow and Queen's University Belfast (1856), later serving in the Indian Civil Service (1857–1893) and as president of The Asiatic Society (1890–1891).

Henry Chung-hung Shiu works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Toronto (completed by 2006), studying under Shek-wing Tam, Leonard C. D. C. Priestley, David Waterhouse, and Willard Gurdon Oxtoby.

Henry Clarke Warren was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Harvard University, Johns Hopkins University, and the University of Oxford under Charles Rockwell Lanman, Maurice Bloomfield, and T. W. Rhys Davids.
